decisions.why: R10 recommendation 1 verbatim: 'A key bundle carries the source's front matter ... and a window around each passage the record quotes from it, not the whole saved page'. Re-run 2026-09-27 (make check-bundle KEY=cdlib-local-elites OUT=/tmp/sfv-cdlib): 22,857 BYTES in two parts (the manifest gives the excerpt as 22,561 characters), every passage the record actually quotes windowed. Its header, however, reads '5 of 8 quoted passage(s) found': quoted_passages also collects three quoted strings from an HTML session comment in cities/hinterland 010's notes, which are not quotations of the source, while D19.1 reports 'all five passages the record quotes from it found'. decisions.summary: The excerpt also reaches source-reader: the write-session brief (brief.py line 151, step 2 'Read the sources') tells the session, for a source already in the registry, to run make check-bundle KEY=<key> and name its MANIFEST to source-reader - which now holds only the front and windows around passages ALREADY quoted.
decisions.why: R10 recommendation 1's purpose, in its own headline: 'A check reads the part of a long source it NEEDS'. The window-around-quotes form was stated for what source-applicability judges; source-reader in a write session needs the passage for a NEW claim, which by construction is not next to an existing quote, and any registered page over 30,000 characters (most long Wikipedia articles) is cut to 6,000 + windows. That narrows the spec's source-reader pass ('read what you cite') and invites a false NOT-FOUND and an absence note where a citation exists - against the GM's stated focus, 'getting the research process right'.
